Delta-method inference for the between-response partial correlations

Source: R/interpret.R
mc_partial_cor_delta.Rd

Attaches standard errors and confidence intervals to the partial correlations of mc_partial_cor by the delta method. The gradient of \(\rho_{ij\mid\mathrm{rest}} = -K_{ij}/\sqrt{K_{ii}K_{jj}}\) with respect to the covariance parameters \(\theta_d\) is $$[\mathbf g_{ij}]_d = -\frac{[\dot{\mathbf K}_d]_{ij}}{\sqrt{K_{ii}K_{jj}}} - \frac{\rho_{ij\mid\mathrm{rest}}}{2}\left\{ \frac{[\dot{\mathbf K}_d]_{ii}}{K_{ii}} + \frac{[\dot{\mathbf K}_d]_{jj}}{K_{jj}}\right\},$$ and the variance follows as \(\mathbf g_{ij}^\top \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat{\boldsymbol\theta})\,\mathbf g_{ij}\) with \(\dot{\mathbf K}_d = \partial\mathbf K_b/\partial\theta_d\). In the GGM layer \(\dot{\mathbf K}_d\) is the canonical base \(\mathbf Z_d\); the implementation obtains it from \(\dot{\mathbf K}_d = -\mathbf K_b \dot{\boldsymbol\Sigma}_d \mathbf K_b\), which holds for any parametrization, so the same expression also covers the DAG layer, where the parameters are \((\boldsymbol\gamma,\boldsymbol\delta)\).

Usage

mc_partial_cor_delta(
  fit,
  variability = c("model", "empirical", "two_stage"),
  cluster = NULL,
  small_sample = FALSE,
  level = 0.95,
  interval = c("wald", "fisher"),
  method = c("auto", "shortcut", "full")
)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph".

variability

"model" for the model-based covariance \(\mathbf J_n^{-1}\), "empirical" for the sandwich form \(\mathbf H_n^{-1}(n\hat{\mathbf V})\mathbf H_n^{-1}\), with \(\mathbf H_n\) the observed curvature of the graph block, or "two_stage" for the sandwich corrected for the estimation of the residuals. When the correction takes the shortcut, the two empirical forms give the partial correlations exactly the same variance, since their gradients annihilate the shortcut's cross sensitivity algebraically; with the full form they agree to first order under the conditions of the section "What the correction reaches" of mc_vcov_graph. Whether that common variance is right depends on the same conditions: a residual correlation that moves with the covariates puts both off, and only the full form accounts for it, which method = "full" requests and method = "auto" takes, when it is available, for a fit with a variance function other than "constant". The model-based form agrees with the empirical ones only when, in addition, \(\mathbf V=\mathbf J\), which fails outside the Gaussian fourth-moment regime.

cluster

optional vector with one identifier per observational row, honored by the two empirical forms ("empirical" and "two_stage"). Contributions are summed within clusters before the variability is formed, which is what to use when the unit of dependence is not the row of the data matrix.

small_sample

logical; multiply the clustered variability by \(G/(G-1)\), with \(G\) the number of clusters (default FALSE).

level

confidence level of the interval, a single number in \((0, 1)\) (default 0.95).

interval

"wald" (default), symmetric on the scale of the partial correlation, or "fisher", symmetric on the scale of \(\operatorname{atanh}(\rho)\), where the standard error is \(\mathrm{se}/(1-\rho^2)\), and mapped back by \(\tanh\), so that the bounds stay inside \((-1, 1)\). The standard error, the statistic and the p-value are the same under both.

method

for variability = "two_stage", the route of the correction, "auto" (default), "shortcut" or "full", as in mc_vcov_graph. It has no meaning for the other two forms and is refused with them when it is not "auto".

Value

A data frame with one row per pair of responses (\(q = R(R-1)/2\) rows) and columns response1, response2, present (logical support indicator), pcor (the partial correlation), se (standard error), statistic (Wald statistic pcor / se, NA when the standard error is exactly zero), p_value (two-sided, normal reference) and lower, upper (interval bounds). A pair with present = FALSE has pcor = 0 and NA in se, statistic, p_value, lower and upper. A pair whose partial correlation is undefined (a nonpositive product of precision diagonals) has NA in pcor and in the same columns. When the covariance of the parameters is not positive semidefinite, se and what follows from it are NA. The rows follow the pairs \((i, j)\), \(i < j\), in lexicographic order. The attribute "gradient" holds the matrix of gradients \(\mathbf g_{ij}\), with one row per pair and one column per graph parameter. The row of a pair with present = FALSE is exactly 0, the gradient of a constant, and the row of a pair with an undefined partial correlation is NA. The attributes "variability", "level" and "interval" record the choices used; with variability = "two_stage" the attribute "two_stage_method" records the route taken.

Scope of the inference

With variability = "model" or "empirical" the variance refers to the second stage conditionally on the estimated residuals: it propagates the uncertainty of the covariance parameters, not the uncertainty inherited from the first-stage fit, which "two_stage" adds. With variability = "model" it also assumes the working identity \(\mathbf V = \mathbf J\); outside the Gaussian fourth-moment regime the empirical option is the appropriate one. Applied to a support chosen by a search over graphs, the interval remains descriptive, since the selection is not incorporated. The function refuses fits whose numerical diagnostics explicitly mark graph-layer inference as uncertified.

Structural zeros

In the GGM layer, a pair outside the specified precision support is zero by construction and has no sampling distribution. Its row reports pcor = 0 and NA for se, statistic, p_value, lower and upper. Its row of the "gradient" attribute is exactly 0 in every column: the partial correlation of such a pair is the constant 0, and the gradient of a constant is 0. That row of zeros is not a standard error of zero: a quadratic form in it gives 0, while the pair has no sampling distribution at all, which is what the NA in se says. All of this is decided from present and not from the size of the standard error. In the DAG layer, structural zeros of the precision are instead determined by the moral graph. In particular, two non-adjacent parents of a common child can have a nonzero precision entry even though no arrow joins them. Therefore present denotes adjacency in the specified GGM support or in the moral graph of the specified DAG. Rows with present = FALSE are structural constraints, not estimates of a null association, and carry no inference; a TRUE value says only that the entry is structurally allowed, since parameter cancellation can still make it zero.

References

Lauritzen, S. L. (1996). Graphical Models. Oxford University Press.

See also

mc_partial_cor for the point estimates, mc_vcov_graph for the covariance of the graph parameters and mc_test_independence for the joint Wald test.

Other graph interpretation: mc_get_graph(), mc_partial_cor(), mc_plot_network()

Examples

set.seed(1); n <- 300
K <- diag(3) * 2; K[1, 2] <- K[2, 1] <- -0.7
Y <- matrix(rnorm(n * 3), n) %*% chol(solve(K))
d <- data.frame(y1 = Y[, 1], y2 = Y[, 2], y3 = Y[, 3], x = rnorm(n))
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1~x, y2~x, y3~x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
mc_partial_cor_delta(f)
#>   response1 response2 present       pcor         se statistic      p_value
#> 1        y1        y2    TRUE 0.34500759 0.05086281 6.7831008 1.176235e-11
#> 2        y1        y3    TRUE 0.02602162 0.05769593 0.4510130 6.519802e-01
#> 3        y2        y3    TRUE 0.04177389 0.05763428 0.7248098 4.685687e-01
#>         lower     upper
#> 1  0.24531830 0.4446969
#> 2 -0.08706033 0.1391036
#> 3 -0.07118722 0.1547350
mc_partial_cor_delta(f, variability = "empirical")
#>   response1 response2 present       pcor         se statistic      p_value
#> 1        y1        y2    TRUE 0.34500759 0.05402660 6.3858832 1.704110e-10
#> 2        y1        y3    TRUE 0.02602162 0.06203153 0.4194902 6.748579e-01
#> 3        y2        y3    TRUE 0.04177389 0.05467196 0.7640826 4.448180e-01
#>         lower     upper
#> 1  0.23911739 0.4508978
#> 2 -0.09555795 0.1476012
#> 3 -0.06538118 0.1489290
